mainTopic: Liability for מעילה when taking, giving or building with הקדש; whether built structures count as attached; and the opening of the new פרק on a שליח and מעילה
overview: This amud finishes a משנה about מעילה, which means using הקדש (Temple) property for personal benefit. The משנה teaches that someone who takes a stone, a beam or a פרוטה of הקדש is not yet liable. He becomes liable once he gives it to a friend, builds it into his house and lives under it, or pays a bathhouse attendant with it. It also teaches that eating and benefit by two people combine to reach a פרוטה. The גמרא explains that the first case is about a גזבר (Temple treasurer), who is supposed to hold these items. רב explains that the building case is about a stone simply laid over a window, with no change made to it. The גמרא then tries twice to prove רב's view that a building made from loose materials still counts as detached. Both proofs are rejected: one with the rule of visible benefit, and one by ריש לקיש, who says the ברייתא is about materials that became הקדש before they were built. After explaining why the ברייתא used a cave as its example, the פרק ends. A new פרק opens with the rule that a שליח who follows his instructions makes the sender liable for מעילה, along with examples.

steps.title: Giving a הקדש stone or beam to a friend, or building it into a house
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues the case of someone who took a stone or beam of הקדש. If he gives it to his friend, he is liable for מעילה and the friend is not. If he builds it into his house, he is not liable until he lives under it for benefit worth a פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he gave it to his friend, he is liable for מעילה and his friend is not. If he built it into his house, he is not liable until he lives under it for benefit worth a פרוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its case of a person who took a stone or beam of הקדש. It now tells us what happens when he hands it to a friend or builds it into his house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just taking the item did not make him liable. Handing it to someone else does make him liable, and the person who receives it is not liable. Building it into his house is not enough by itself; he becomes liable only once he actually lives under it and gets benefit worth a פרוטה.

keyTerms.meaning: He has committed מעילה, meaning he misused הקדש property and is liable for it
His fellow, meaning another person
That he will live beneath it
Worth a פרוטה, the smallest amount that creates liability for מעילה

phrases.english: If he gave it to his fellow,
phrases.notes: "It" is the stone or beam of הקדש from the line just before this, which he took without yet being liable.

phrases.english: he has committed misuse, and his fellow has not committed misuse.
If he built it into his house,
he has not committed misuse,
until he lives beneath it to the value of a perutah.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְתָנָהּ לַחֲבֵרוֹ – הוּא מָעַל, וַחֲבֵרוֹ לֹא מָעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's case of taking a stone or beam of הקדש, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Giving the item to another makes the giver liable, not the receiver. Building it into one's house creates liability only after living under it for a פרוטה's worth of benefit.

steps.title: Taking a פרוטה of הקדש and giving it away or paying a bathhouse attendant
steps.stepSummary: Taking a פרוטה of הקדש does not make one liable. Giving it to a friend makes the giver liable and not the friend. Giving it to a בלן makes him liable even if he never bathes, because the bathhouse is now open to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he took a פרוטה of הקדש, he is not liable. If he gave it to his friend, he is liable and his friend is not. If he gave it to a bathhouse attendant, he is liable even though he did not bathe, because the attendant tells him: the bathhouse is open to you, go in and bathe.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה applies the same rule to a coin, a פרוטה of הקדש. It adds a new case of paying a bathhouse attendant with that coin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The coin works like the stone or beam: taking it is not yet מעילה, but handing it over is. The bathhouse case teaches that he does not need to actually bathe. The moment he pays, he has gotten something worth a פרוטה, because the bathhouse is open to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Property that belongs to the Temple
A bathhouse attendant, who takes payment for entry
A bathhouse

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think he is liable only if he actually bathes. The משנה says he is liable as soon as he pays, because entry is now available to him.

phrases.english: If he took a perutah of consecrated property,
he has not committed misuse.
If he gave it to his fellow,
he has committed misuse, and his fellow has not committed misuse.
If he gave it to a bathhouse attendant,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא רָחַץ מָעַל,
phrases.english: even though he did not bathe, he has committed misuse,
because he says to him:
phrases.notes: "He" here is the attendant, speaking to the man who paid him.

phrases.english: Here, the bathhouse is open before you,
go in and bathe.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָטַל פְּרוּטָה שֶׁל הֶקְדֵּשׁ – הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא מָעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the stone-and-beam rule to a coin and adds the bathhouse case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Paying a בלן with a הקדש פרוטה is מעילה right away, because the open bathhouse is already a benefit worth a פרוטה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that benefit can be counted by what becomes available to a person, not only by what he actually uses.

steps.title: Eating and benefit by two people combine to a פרוטה
steps.stepSummary: Eating or benefit by one person, together with eating or benefit by his friend, in any combination, join to make up a פרוטה for מעילה, even over a long period of time.
steps.simpleTranslation: His eating and his friend's eating, his benefit and his friend's benefit, his eating and his friend's benefit, his benefit and his friend's eating, all combine together, even over a long time.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה teaches that small amounts of eating and benefit from הקדש can add up to the full פרוטה needed for מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are four combinations: eating plus eating, benefit plus benefit, and both mixed pairs. All of them combine, even if the two people are different and even if a long time passes between the acts. So the פרוטה minimum can be reached through pieces.

keyTerms.meaning: Eating
Benefit, any use or enjoyment that is not eating
They combine, adding up to reach a required amount
Over a long period of time

steps.whatToRemember: For מעילה, eating and benefit, by one person or two, combine to reach a פרוטה, with no time limit.

phrases.english: His eating and his fellow's eating,
phrases.notes: Picture each one using half a פרוטה's worth; together they make the full פרוטה.

phrases.english: his benefit and his fellow's benefit,
his eating and his fellow's benefit,
his benefit and his fellow's eating,
combine with one another,
and even over a long period of time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the משנה with a new rule about combining amounts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating and benefit, by one person and his friend, in any combination, join to a פרוטה even over a long time.

steps.title: Why does giving the item away change the outcome?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is puzzled by the first case of the משנה: why is the person not liable when he takes the item, but liable once he gives it to his friend?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is different about him keeping it, and what is different about giving it to his friend?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a puzzle about the משנה's first case. This sets up שמואל's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking הקדש property for yourself sounds like a misuse already, so it is strange that he is liable only when he passes it on. The גמרא wants to know what makes handing it over different from just holding it.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that follows and analyzes the משנה
What is different? Used to ask why two cases are treated differently

phrases.english: Gemara: What is different about him,
and what is different about his fellow?!
phrases.notes: He means: why is keeping it himself not מעילה, while giving it to his friend is?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא הוּא, וּמַאי שְׁנָא חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the first ruling of the משנה (step 1) and questions its logic.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that taking a stone or beam of הקדש is not מעילה, but giving it to a friend is.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If taking הקדש for himself is not misuse, why does passing it to someone else suddenly make him liable? The difference seems to have no reason.

steps.title: שמואל: the case is a Temple treasurer
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that the משנה is talking about a גזבר, a Temple treasurer, who is in charge of הקדש property.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: We are dealing with a גזבר, to whom these items are entrusted.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the puzzle by saying which person the משנה is describing: the גזבר, who looks after הקדש property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The items are already supposed to be in the גזבר's hands. So when he takes one, nothing has left הקדש's control, and there is no מעילה. When he hands it to someone else, he takes it out of הקדש's control, and that is when he becomes liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Temple treasurer, in charge of הקדש property
Which are entrusted to him
We are dealing with this case

steps.whatToRemember: According to שמואל, the משנה's first case is about a גזבר. Holding הקדש items is his job, so only giving them away counts as מעילה.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
We are dealing with a treasurer, to whom they are entrusted.
phrases.notes: "They" are the הקדש items, like the stone and beam in the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: בְּגִזְבָּר, הַמְּסוּרוֹת לוֹ, עָסְקִינַן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to a specific kind of person
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the משנה was about any ordinary person, so it made no sense that taking was not misuse but giving was.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a גזבר who is in charge of the items. Holding them is normal for him, and only giving them away removes them from הקדש.

steps.title: Why wait until he lives under it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about building a הקדש stone into one's house and asks why liability waits until he lives under it, since changing the stone should already be מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if he built it into his house, he is not liable until he lives under it. Why do we need 'until he lives under it'? Once he changed the stone to build with it, he has already committed מעילה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and challenges it. Building usually means shaping the stone, and changing הקדש property is already מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When someone changes a הקדש object for his own use, he has already done מעילה. Fitting a stone or beam into a wall normally requires shaping it. So the משנה's condition, 'until he lives under it', seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: He changed it (altered the object, such as shaping it)
Why do I need this? Asks why a detail is needed

phrases.aramaic: בְּנָאָהּ בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ – אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: If he built it into his house, he is not liable, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה from Step 1. The 'etc.' stands for 'until he lives under it and gets a פרוטה's worth of benefit.'

phrases.english: Why do I need 'until he lives beneath it'?
Once he has changed it, he has committed misuse!
phrases.notes: To build a stone or beam into a wall, you usually have to shape or cut it first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first case of the משנה (giving to a friend, Steps 4-5) to the second case (building into a house).
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that liability begins only once he lives beneath the stone or beam.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Changing הקדש property is already מעילה, and building normally involves changing the material. So liability should start at the moment of building.

steps.title: He just laid it over a window opening
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that the משנה is talking about someone who placed the stone or beam over an opening without changing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: The case is where he just laid it over the opening of a window.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question by narrowing the case. The person did not shape the stone. He just set it in place over an opening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Simply placing an object is not a change, so there is no מעילה at that moment. Liability only comes once he actually benefits by living under it. That is why the משנה needs 'until he lives beneath it.'

keyTerms.meaning: For example; the case is where
An opening, such as a window or skylight

phrases.english: Rav said:
For example, where he placed it over the opening of a window.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהִנִּיחָהּ עַל פִּי אֲרוּבָּה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Building means shaping the stone, so מעילה should happen right away.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is talking about simply placing it over an opening with no change, so liability waits until he benefits by living under it.
steps.whatToRemember: No change at the moment of building means no מעילה until he actually benefits by living beneath it.

steps.title: Does this support רב on bowing to a house?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that once it is built in, he is still liable, and suggests this supports רב's ruling that a house someone bows to becomes forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And once he has built it in, in any case he commits מעילה. Shall we say this supports רב? For רב said: someone who bows down to a house has made it forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the stone counts for מעילה even after it becomes part of a building. It tries to use this as proof for another ruling of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, things attached to the ground are not subject to מעילה, and they do not become forbidden through עבודה זרה. Our משנה treats a stone built into a house as still subject to מעילה, so built materials are still treated like detached objects. That matches רב's ruling that a house someone worships becomes forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case; at least
Shall we say this supports him?
One who bows down (as an act of עבודה זרה)
He has made it forbidden (for any benefit)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב is talking about bowing to a house in a normal, harmless way. The case is worshipping the house as עבודה זרה. The question is whether a building counts as 'attached to the ground', which would keep it from becoming forbidden.

phrases.english: And once he builds it in, in any case he has committed misuse.
Shall we say this supports Rav,
as Rav said:
One who bows down to a house has made it forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the conclusion of Step 7, that the built-in stone is subject to מעילה, as a possible proof for a separate ruling of רב.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that one who bows to a house makes it forbidden, meaning built materials keep the status of detached objects.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: a הקדש stone built into a house is still subject to מעילה once he lives under it.

steps.title: The Torah forbids benefit you can see
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא rejects the proof. מעילה here comes from a different reason: the Torah forbade visible benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רב איקא said: The Torah forbade benefit that is visible to the eyes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא pushes back on the proof from Step 8. He gives another reason why the built-in stone is subject to מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if a building counts as attached to the ground, using a הקדש stone as part of your house is obvious, visible benefit. The Torah forbade that kind of benefit regardless of the attachment question. So the משנה says nothing about bowing to a house, and it gives no support to רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Benefit that can be seen with the eyes; obvious, visible use
The Torah forbade

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa, son of Rav Ika, said:
Benefit that is visible to the eyes
the Torah forbade.
phrases.notes: He means: for מעילה, visible benefit like living under a הקדש beam is forbidden even if the beam counts as attached.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in Step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof only. It does not argue that רב's ruling is wrong.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's liability can be explained by the rule of visible benefit, without deciding that built materials count as detached.

steps.title: A second proof: living in a הקדש house
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: someone who lives in a הקדש house commits מעילה once he benefits. This seems to show a built house counts as detached.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this supports him: One who lives in a house that is הקדש commits מעילה once he benefits from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries again to support רב, this time from a ברייתא about a whole house belonging to הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a building were treated as attached to the ground, there should be no מעילה on it. The ברייתא says there is מעילה. So it seems a built house keeps the status of a detached object, just as רב holds.

keyTerms.meaning: A house that belongs to the Temple treasury
He benefited

phrases.english: Shall we say this supports him:
One who lives in a house of הקדש,
once he has benefited from it, he has committed misuse.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ: הַדָּר בְּבַיִת שֶׁל הֶקְדֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected in Step 9, the גמרא offers a new proof for רב.
steps.raayaObject: רב's view that something built from detached materials keeps the status of a detached object.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: one who lives in a הקדש house commits מעילה once he benefits.

steps.title: There, it was made הקדש before it was built
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש rejects the proof. The ברייתא is talking about materials that became הקדש while still loose and were only built into a house later.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: There, it is where he made it הקדש first and only afterward built it.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש pushes back on the second proof. He narrows the ברייתא to a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the materials became הקדש while they were still loose, they already had full מעילה status. Building them into a house afterward does not remove it. The ברייתא therefore says nothing about whether a building counts as detached, so it gives no support to רב.

keyTerms.meaning: There (in that source)
He made it הקדש first and built it afterward

steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs for רב are rejected. The built-in stone is explained by 'visible benefit', and the הקדש house is explained by the materials becoming הקדש before being built.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
There, it is where he made it הקדש
and only afterward built it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: הָתָם בְּשֶׁהִקְדִּישׁוֹ וּלְבַסּוֹף בְּנָאוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in Step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the ברייתא. רב's ruling itself is left unproven but not refuted.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be read as a case where the materials became הקדש while detached, so it does not show that a built house counts as detached.

steps.title: Why Mention a Cave Instead of a Built House?
steps.stepSummary: If a house built first and sanctified later has no מעילה, the ברייתא should have used that example instead of a cave.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he built the house and only afterward sanctified it, what is the law? He has not committed מעילה, right? So why does the תנא go out of his way to teach the case of someone living in a cave house who has not committed מעילה? Let him just say: someone living in a stone house that was built and then sanctified has not committed מעילה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש's reading of the ברייתא. If only loose materials that were later built into a house bring מעילה, then a house built first and sanctified later should have no מעילה, so why did the ברייתא pick a cave as its example?
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to ריש לקיש, a house that was already attached to the ground when it was sanctified is like ground, and there is no מעילה for ground. That makes a built-then-sanctified house a natural contrast to the first case in the ברייתא. Choosing a cave instead seems strange, and that is the question.

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically this case? Why pick this example?
He runs and teaches, meaning he goes out of his way to teach
A cave dwelling, which was never made of loose parts
He built it first and only afterward sanctified it

steps.confusionAlert: This is not just a question about style. The rule that a built-then-sanctified house has no מעילה comes from ריש לקיש's own distinction. If that distinction were right, the ברייתא should have used the stone house as its example. So the odd choice of a cave is really a challenge to ריש לקיש's reading.

phrases.english: But if he built it and afterward sanctified it,
what is the law? He has not committed misuse?
Why does he go out of his way to teach

phrases.aramaic: הַדָּר בְּבַיִת שֶׁל מְעָרָה – לֹא מָעַל.
phrases.english: one who lives in a cave house has not committed misuse.
Let him say: one who lives in a stone house
that he built and afterward sanctified has not committed misuse!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא's wording based on ריש לקיש's answer in Step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's reading of the ברייתא, and the ברייתא's choice of the cave example
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If built-then-sanctified houses have no מעילה, that was the obvious contrast case, so the cave example looks unnecessary

steps.title: The Cave Is Clear-Cut, the House Is Not
steps.stepSummary: The תנא chose the cave because a cave never brings מעילה, while a house sometimes does.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: this case, the cave, is clear-cut for him. That case, the house, is not clear-cut for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The ברייתא picked the cave because it is a rule with no exceptions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A cave was always attached to the ground, so living in a הקדש cave never brings מעילה. A house is different: if it was built from loose materials that were already הקדש, living in it does bring מעילה. So a house does not make a clean example, and the תנא preferred the case that is always true.

keyTerms.meaning: It is clear-cut for him, meaning the rule holds every time with no exceptions
It is not clear-cut, meaning the outcome depends on the details

steps.whatToRemember: There is no מעילה for something attached to the ground, like a cave or a house sanctified after it was built. But if loose items became הקדש and were then built into a house, using that house is מעילה. The ברייתא picked the cave because it is the case with no exceptions.

phrases.english: They say: this one is clear-cut for him,
phrases.notes: "This one" is the cave. It was always part of the ground, so there is never מעילה.

phrases.english: that one is not clear-cut for him.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the תנא's choice of example: he prefers a case whose rule has no exceptions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The built house was the better contrast case, so the cave example seemed unnecessary
steps.terutzMaskana: The cave is always free of מעילה, while a house depends on when its materials became הקדש, so the תנא used the cave

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the Chapter of הנהנה
steps.stepSummary: The פרק called הנהנה ends here.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק הנהנה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional line said at the end of a פרק. It closes פרק הנהנה before a new פרק begins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is not part of the argument. It marks the end of the chapter and expresses the hope to come back and learn it again.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you, the closing words said at the end of a פרק
"One who benefits," the name of the chapter that just ended

phrases.english: We will return to you, "One Who Benefits"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formally closes the chapter after the last discussion

steps.title: Who Is Liable When a Messenger Uses הקדש
steps.stepSummary: The new פרק opens: if a שליח follows his instructions, the sender is liable for מעילה, but if he changes them, the שליח is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: A messenger who carried out his mission: the homeowner who sent him is liable for מעילה. If he did not carry out his mission: the messenger is liable for מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins with a משנה. It teaches who is responsible for מעילה when someone sends a שליח to use something that turns out to be הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the שליח does exactly what he was told, his act counts as the sender's act, so the בעל הבית is liable. If the שליח changes the instructions, he is no longer acting for the sender, so he carries the מעילה himself.

keyTerms.meaning: A messenger or agent sent to act for someone else
His mission, the task he was sent to do
The homeowner, here the one who sent the שליח

steps.confusionAlert: In most of the Torah, a sender is not responsible when his שליח does an עבירה. Here by מעילה the sender is liable, but only when the שליח followed his instructions.
steps.whyThisMatters: This opening rule sets up the whole new פרק, which works through cases of when a שליח stays a שליח and when he does not.

phrases.english: A messenger who carried out his mission:
the homeowner has committed misuse.
If he did not carry out his mission:
the messenger has committed misuse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק after the הדרן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שליח who follows instructions makes the sender liable for מעילה; a שליח who changes instructions is liable himself

steps.title: Example: The agent swaps meat and liver
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks 'how so?' and answers: if the owner said 'give meat' and the שליח gave liver, or the reverse, the שליח is the one liable for מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does this work? If the owner told him, 'Give meat to the guests,' and he gave them liver, or the owner said 'liver' and he gave them meat, the agent has committed מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives a concrete example of its rule that a שליח who changes his instructions becomes liable instead of the sender.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner asked for one specific thing and the שליח did something different. Because the שליח acted on his own, the act is his and not the owner's. So the שליח, and not the owner, is liable for מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? This opens an explanation of the rule just stated.
Guests

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the change has to be to something worth more or less. Swapping meat for liver in either direction counts as changing the instructions.

phrases.english: How so?
He said to him: "Give meat to the guests,"
and he gave them liver;
or he said "liver," and he gave them meat
the agent has committed מעילה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an example of the second half of the rule in Step 15, where a שליח who changes his instructions is liable himself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שליח who gives liver instead of meat, or meat instead of liver, is liable for מעילה.

steps.title: One piece, take two, they took three: everyone is liable
steps.stepSummary: The owner said to give one piece each, the שליח told the guests to take two, and they took three. All of them are liable for מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the owner said, 'Give them one piece each,' and the agent said to the guests, 'Take two each,' and they took three each, all of them have committed מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case, where the owner, the שליח, and the guests each add a step, so all three are liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual explanation is that each person is liable for his own part. The owner is liable for the first piece, since the שליח carried out that part of his instructions. The שליח is liable for the second piece he added, and the guests are liable for the third piece they took on their own.

keyTerms.meaning: One piece each
Take (said to several people)
All of them have committed מעילה

steps.whatToRemember: Liability follows the person who made the decision. When the שליח follows orders, the sender is liable. When someone adds on his own, he is liable for what he added. So one act of serving can make several people liable.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that agency is not all-or-nothing. It can be split into parts, with each person liable for the part he chose to do.
